answer: Anchor identities in hardware. An answer counts only with a fresh per-epoch TEE quote binding its key to a chip serial; an auditable public registry grants one live credential per serial per epoch, so a key cannot wander between accounts and identities never exceed chips owned. The nebula of self-declared keys condenses into a checkable count. Each clone needs a rented chip (cost c/epoch): even seizing the whole pool R, profit dies past R/c devices. The velvet promise of non-exportable keys is decoration; the serial rule enforces. Assumes the issuer signs only real chips; chip farms remain.
